entries.text: MessagePack for C# is a fast MessagePack binary serializer with built-in LZ4 compression support.
The library targets .NET Standard 2.0 with special optimizations for .NET 8+ and .NET Framework, and uses either runtime IL generation or AOT-safe source generators.
The MessagePackAnalyzer NuGet package provides compiler warnings, code fixes, and optional AOT formatter generation.
Users annotate their types with [MessagePackObject] and members with [Key], and call MessagePackSerializer.Serialize/Deserialize.
Users who want Json.NET-like behavior without attributes can use the ContractlessStandardResolver.
Contributors build with Visual Studio 2022 or 'dotnet build /p:platform=NoVSIX', and install the required SDKs by running init.ps1.
Maintainers publish releases by running the GitHub Actions workflow_dispatch workflow with a version tag starting with v.
If all keys are integer indexes the object serializes as a MessagePack array, otherwise as a map with string keys.
Gaps in integer key sequences are filled with null placeholders in the array, and indexes of removed members should not be reused.
Serializable types must be public by default and need [MessagePackObject], and keyAsPropertyName: true makes members use their property names as string keys without [Key].
MsgPack003, 004, 005, 006, 007, 008, 009, 011, 012, 016 and 018 are Errors, while MsgPack010, 013, 014, 015 and 017 are Warnings.
MsgPack004 requires public members of [MessagePackObject] types to have either [Key] or [IgnoreMember].
MessagePackKnownFormatterAttribute and MessagePackAssumedFormattableAttribute are assembly-level attributes that suppress analyzer warnings for types with custom formatters.
MsgPack001 and MsgPack002 are Disabled by default in the rule table.
Missing keys during deserialization leave members at their default value, so reference-type members can be null.
Requiring the MessagePackObject annotation by default is intentional, to enforce explicitness.
MsgPack017 warns that an init property initializer's default is replaced by the type's default value on deserialization.
Source generated formatters do not support everything dynamic formatters do, which is why MsgPack008 and MsgPack016 exist.
Recent history includes secure-by-default changes, a collision-resistant hash for untrusted data, a stack depth limit of 500 even for trusted data, and a revert to v2's insecure-by-default mode.
Recent fixes to serializing BigInteger, Decimal, long numbers, and float SIMD show numeric serialization is bug-prone.
Source generator and TypeCollector logic has had many recent fixes, including name collisions, nested types, generic constraints, and recursive constraints that caused a stack overflow.
Analyzer diagnostics such as MsgPack003 and MsgPack004 have recently been adjusted for false positives, so changes can cause wrong reports.
The release CI workflows and the NUGET_KEY secret (which expires after 365 days) are recently changed and operationally sensitive.

Areas allowed: product, annotations, serializer, generator, analyzer, security, build, docs. 2 to 8 bullets per section,
